title: Explain polymorphism (compile-time overloading vs runtime overriding) with examples and why it is useful.
shortTitle: What is polymorphism and why is it useful?
keyPoints: Polymorphism means one call, many behaviors depending on the actual object type
Compile-time polymorphism (overloading): compiler picks by argument types (static dispatch)
Runtime polymorphism (overriding): JVM dispatches to the actual object's method (dynamic dispatch via vtable)
Eliminates growing if-else and switch chains by letting each type handle its own behavior
Enables the Open/Closed Principle: add new types without modifying existing code
Powers the Strategy pattern: swap behavior at runtime by injecting different implementations

s1_definition.oneliner: Polymorphism means one call, many behaviors. Compile-time: overloading (compiler picks by args). Runtime: overriding (JVM picks by actual type). It eliminates if-else chains, enables the Open/Closed Principle, and powers the Strategy pattern.
s1_definition.profdef:
Polymorphism means many forms: one interface, multiple implementations.

- **Compile-time polymorphism** (method overloading): same name, different parameters. The compiler picks the matching signature based on argument types at compile time.
- **Runtime polymorphism** (method overriding): same signature in parent and child. The JVM picks the correct version based on the actual object type at runtime via the vtable.
- **Benefit 1**: eliminates growing `if-else` and `switch` chains by letting each type handle its own behavior.
- **Benefit 2**: enables the Open/Closed Principle, where you add new types without modifying existing code.
- **Benefit 3**: powers the Strategy pattern, where you swap behavior at runtime by injecting different implementations.
- **Benefit 4**: enables generic processing, where one loop handles all types polymorphically.
s1_definition.analogy: The bank's notification system needs to send messages: SMS for savings customers, email for premium customers, push for mobile customers. Without polymorphism: if (type == "SMS") sendSms(); else if (type == "EMAIL") sendEmail(); else if (type == "PUSH") sendPush(); and the chain grows with every new channel. With polymorphism: notificationChannel.send(message). One call. The JVM picks the right implementation at runtime. Adding WhatsApp: create WhatsAppChannel implements NotificationChannel. Zero changes to existing code.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  WITHOUT POLYMORPHISM
  ┌─────────────────────────┐
  │  if (type == SAVINGS)    │
  │    calculateSavingsFee() │
  │  else if (type == CURRENT)│
  │    calculateCurrentFee() │
  │  else if (type == NRI)   │
  │    calculateNriFee()     │
  │  else if ...             │  <- grows with every new type
  └─────────────────────────┘

  WITH POLYMORPHISM
  ┌─────────────────────────┐
  │  account.calculateFee()  │  <- one line
  │         │                │
  │         ▼                │
  │  JVM dispatches to:      │
  │  ├─ SavingsAccount: 0.1% │
  │  ├─ CurrentAccount: 0.2% │
  │  ├─ NRIAccount: 0.3%     │
  │  └─ FDAccount: 0%        │  <- new type, zero changes
  └─────────────────────────┘
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Polymorphism means many forms: one interface, multiple implementations. Compile-time polymorphism is method overloading: same name, different parameters, compiler picks. Runtime polymorphism is method overriding: same signature, different classes, JVM picks based on actual object type. Runtime polymorphism is the more powerful form because it enables four critical production benefits: eliminating growing if-else chains, Open/Closed Principle (add types without modifying existing code), Strategy pattern (swap behavior at runtime via injection), and generic processing (one loop handles all types).

In Pankaj's notification dispatch service at National Bank of India, channel.send(recipient, message) dispatches to SmsChannel, EmailChannel, PushChannel, or WhatsAppChannel at runtime. One line replaces a 200-line switch statement. When WhatsApp was added: one new class implementing the interface, one bean registration. NotificationDispatcher: zero lines changed. Existing channels: zero lines changed. Existing tests: still pass.

Remember one sentence: polymorphism eliminates conditional logic and enables extension without modification, which is the foundation of maintainable software.
